en.title: Fitting Rotatable Rectangles One by One into Query Boxes
en.description:
Execute two kinds of operations in order: `0 a b` stores an a×b rectangle; `1 a b` asks whether every previously stored rectangle can individually fit into an a×b query box. Rectangles may be rotated 90 degrees; each rectangle is placed separately, and they do not need to fit into the same box at the same time.

Standard input/output, this site's supplementary ranges, and the examples follow this problem's description.
en.input: The first line contains q (1≤q≤30000), followed by q lines each containing kind, a, and b. kind is 0 or 1, and 1≤a,b≤10⁹. These ranges are site supplements that keep the worst-case output length within the judge's limit.
en.output: Output one line per query operation: 1 if they fit, otherwise 0. When no rectangles have been stored, the query result is 1.
en.explanation: Normalize the sides of both the rectangles and the query boxes into a short side and a long side. Maintain the maximum short side and the maximum long side over all stored rectangles; a query box can hold every rectangle if and only if these two maxima do not exceed the corresponding sides of the box.
hints: Normalize the sides of both the rectangles and the query boxes into a short side and a long side. Maintain the maximum short side and the maximum long side over all stored rectangles; a query box can hold every rectangle if and only if these two maxima do not exceed the corresponding sides of the box.
